source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, banana cultivation techniques manual, 2019, section V.1.5 (bunchy top virus)
text:
Banana Bunchy Top Virus is transmitted by the banana aphid (Pentalonia nigronervosa) while it feeds on plant sap. Infected plants become stunted and produce small, narrow, distorted leaves that bunch tightly together at the crown, giving the plant a "cabbage-like" appearance; affected plants generally fail to produce a usable bunch of fruit.

There is no cure once a plant is infected, so management is entirely preventive: control the aphid vector population, use only disease-free planting material sourced from healthy stock, and promptly remove and destroy any plant showing bunchy-top symptoms so it cannot serve as a source of virus for aphids to spread to neighboring healthy plants in the same clump or field.
